title: The Generalized-cμ Rule at a Job-Shop Bottleneck with Family Setups: Analysis, Simulation, and a Setup-Aware Variant
content: The generalized-cμ (Gcμ) rule is asymptotically optimal for a single multiclass queue with convex delay costs, no setups and traffic intensity near one. We ask what it is worth when applied only at the bottleneck of a job shop with family setup times. Without setups and with equal service rates, its heavy-traffic cost ratio to FIFO has the closed form 1/[(∑iπi/ai)(∑iπiai)], equal to 0.66 for our shop and confirmed by simulation. In a two-class model the rule gains more over FIFO as setups grow, because it switches families less often; we derive the switching frequency exactly for a saturated chain. Against a setup-aware, weights-aware heuristic, in a simulation of a five-machine job shop from the literature, the rule’s advantage disappears at setup-to-processing ratios of about 0.1. A hysteresis variant extends the window to about 0.25, and in some variants 0.5, with gains of 3–12%; it beats a tuned limited-batching rule by 4–8%, but weighted shop flow time is 1–2% worse. Most benchmark instances and the one real-plant instance we found have ratios of 1 to 5, where the index rules lose 4–10%. The rule suits bottlenecks with small setups.
